categories.main_business_segments: The Clorox Company operates through four reportable segments: Health and Wellness (cleaning, disinfecting, and professional products sold in the U.S.), Household (bags, wraps, cat litter, and grilling products in the U.S.), Lifestyle (food, water-filtration, and natural personal care products in the U.S.), and International (products sold outside the U.S.). The company is a leading multinational manufacturer and marketer of consumer and professional products with fiscal year 2024 net sales of $7.1 billion.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company manufactures cleaning and disinfecting products, bags and wraps, cat litter, grilling products, food products, water-filtration systems, and natural personal care products. Core technologies include formulation of bleach-based and non-bleach cleaning products, polymer-based bag and wrap manufacturing, and water-filtration technology. The company is undergoing a multi-year digital transformation including replacement of its enterprise resource planning system and transitioning to a cloud-based platform.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company sells primarily to mass retailers, grocery outlets, warehouse clubs, dollar stores, home hardware centers, drug stores, pet stores, military stores, and through e-commerce channels. Major end markets include household cleaning, professional cleaning and disinfecting, food service, pet care, and dietary supplements. Walmart and its affiliates represent 25% of consolidated net sales, and the five largest customers account for nearly half of total sales.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company has operations in approximately 25 countries or territories and sells products in more than 100 markets. In fiscal year 2024, 84% of net sales were attributable to U.S. markets including U.S. territories, while 16% came from international markets. The company has a significant presence in North America and operates internationally through subsidiaries, licensees, distributors, and joint-venture arrangements.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates as a midstream to downstream player in the consumer products supply chain. It manufactures finished consumer and professional products and distributes them through multiple retail channels directly to consumers and businesses. The company sources raw materials from numerous suppliers and relies on a complex global network of suppliers for commodities, packaging, and components.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company's IGNITE strategy focuses on four strategic choices: fueling long-term profitable growth, innovating consumer experiences, reimagining how the company and its people work, and continuously evolving the product portfolio. Key R&D initiatives include developing new product innovations (such as new Hidden Valley flavors, Pine-Sol concentrated cleaners, and Brita refillable systems), advancing digital capabilities, and implementing a streamlined operating model. The company also prioritizes ESG goals including greenhouse gas emission reductions and reducing plastic and waste.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through direct product sales to retailers and distributors across multiple channels including mass retail, grocery, warehouse clubs, dollar stores, e-commerce, and direct-to-consumer channels. Revenue is derived from four reportable segments with approximately 80% of sales from brands holding No. 1 or No. 2 market share positions. The company also generates revenue from professional products sold to institutional, janitorial, food-service, and healthcare customers.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company faces intense competition from other nationally advertised brands, private label brands, and retailers offering store brands. Competitors include major multinational and national companies with potentially greater financial resources. The company competes on product performance, brand reputation and recognition, image, and price. About 80% of the company's sales come from brands in No. 1 or No. 2 market share positions in their categories, indicating strong competitive positioning.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: The Clorox Company is a large multinational corporation with fiscal year 2024 net sales of $7.1 billion and approximately 8,000 employees worldwide. The company is a large accelerated filer on the New York Stock Exchange (ticker: CLX) with a market capitalization of approximately $17.7 billion as of December 29, 2023. The company has demonstrated resilience, recovering from a significant cyberattack in August 2023 while rebuilding gross margins through pricing actions and cost savings.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company's value proposition centers on trusted, recognized brand names with strong market positions and proven efficacy in cleaning, disinfecting, food, pet care, and wellness categories. Key differentiators include: market-leading brands (Clorox, Glad, Hidden Valley, Brita, Burt's Bees), approximately 80% of sales from No. 1 or No. 2 market share brands, commitment to innovation and product development, strong distribution network across multiple retail channels, and integrated ESG initiatives. The company emphasizes quality, safety, and sustainability in its products and operations.
